name: prior-standards
description: Our former forms and the standard history (OPF-SPEC §3.5.7, §3.12.2, issue #249). Three forms are supplied (baseline.prior_templates, with the content address and any dates the owner gave). Five of six deals' clauses opened on something of ours or a counterparty's: deal-a and deal-d opened on the 2018 form and signed it as it stood (opened_with prior_standard, opened_with_form 2018 form, no distinct opening_text: kept), deal-b opened on it and moved to today's standard (opening_text recorded, standard true), deal-c opened on the 2019 form and ended on a variant (conceded), deal-e opened with today's standard, and deal-f opened with the counterparty's own text (non_standard). The clause counts n_opened_prior 4, n_kept_prior 2 and n_moved_to_current 1 are derived from those records, and n_changed_openings is 1: only deal-f's opening is a counterparty ask, our own former wording never is. Each form's clause is judged once against today's two parts (role prior_standard, the same cache key as any text): the 2018 form's judgment is also the verdict of the two deals that signed its words. The 2021 form reads exactly as today's standard, so it is unchanged with no part map. The digest's standard_history lists the forms in config order with their in-use dates (config for the 2018 form, the config start and the latest signing month of its deals for the 2019 form: mixed, only the config start for the 2021 form), the opened, kept, conceded and moved-to-current deals, the part map against today's standard, and the form's own parts (null where the passage is today's); why_changed is the owner's note, the only reason ever given. Each form's clause is cited in that form's own bytes (document_id prior_template:<label>, version prior_template, resolved through the form's baseline.prior_templates sha256), never as template, which is today's form.

part_map.=: our part is present with the same legal effect
part_map.+: our part is present but more protective for perspective.party
part_map.-: our part is present but less protective for perspective.party
part_map.x+: our part is omitted, which is more protective for perspective.party
part_map.x-: our part is omitted, which is less protective for perspective.party
part_map.x0: our part is omitted with no effect on perspective.party

additions.+: an addition no part covers, more protective for perspective.party
additions.-: an addition no part covers, less protective for perspective.party
additions.0: an addition no part covers, neutral for perspective.party

label_by.parts: the default, so a digest entry omits label_by: the label is derived from the part map and additions; reason is the judgment's most important difference
label_by.owner: the owner set the label over the judged part map and additions, which may imply another label; reason is the owner's and wins

settled.agreed: an independent blind check reached the same label and parts as the judgment
settled.adjudicated: the blind check disagreed and a fresh agent decided: the judgment shown is that decision, so this label was contested and deserves more scrutiny
settled.unchecked: no completed blind check (none yet, or a disagreement still awaiting adjudication): weaker evidence than agreed or adjudicated
settled.owner: the owner set or corrected the judgment; it is never blind-checked
